question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[{e}^{X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{1-x}}{e(e-1)},\,-1\le x\le 0.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={e}^{x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{e}^{X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{{e}^{1-x}}{e(e-1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{e}{e(e-1)}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{\cancel{e}}{\cancel{e}(e-1)}\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{x}{e-1}]}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{e-1}.\end{aligned}
$$
